learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of expressing yourself clearly and listening deeply! Learn how to break down barriers and communicate like a leader.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Verbal communication uses words (speaking or writing). Non-verbal communication happens without words—through facial expressions, body language, eye contact, and tone of voice. Often, our body language speaks louder than our words.
Communication is a loop: A Sender encodes a message -> sends it through a Channel -> the Receiver decodes it -> and finally gives Feedback to confirm understanding.
Hearing is just a physical process, but 'listening' is a mental process. Active listening involves paying full attention, not interrupting, and responding appropriately to show you understand.

Things that ruin a message are called barriers. They can be Physical (loud background noise), Psychological (anger, prejudice), or Semantic (using difficult words or a language the receiver doesn't know).
Empathy is putting yourself in someone else's shoes. Effective communicators are empathetic; they adjust their message based on the feelings and understanding of the listener.

fun_activity.title: 🤷‍♀️ The Silent Movie Game
fun_activity.instructions: Try to communicate an emotion (like 'I am extremely nervous about my exam') to a friend without using a single word. See if they can guess it just by your posture and facial expressions!

exam_tips: 📌 Always include 'Feedback' when explaining the communication cycle. Without feedback, communication is incomplete.
📌 Give practical examples of non-verbal communication, like nodding, crossing arms, or maintaining eye contact.
📌 Identify the 3 types of barriers: Physical (noise), Psychological (emotions), and Semantic (language/vocabulary).
quick_recap: ⭐ Good communication is about clarity, respect, and listening.
⭐ Tone of voice can completely change the meaning of the words you say.
⭐ Asking clarifying questions is a sign of an active listener.
